skills.name: Upjohn
skills.description: Properly identifies representation and role with the Company, and that they cannot give the employee legal advice. This must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.
skills.reason: At T2 the interviewer states the Committee and company are the clients, that counsel does not represent the witness personally, is not his attorney and cannot give him legal advice, before substantive questions begin.

skills.name: Privilege
skills.description: Properly explains that the Company controls the privilege and determines how it is shared.
skills.reason: T2 explains that the privilege belongs to the company, that the company decides whether to waive it, and that it may disclose what was learned without the witness's consent.

skills.name: Relationship
skills.description: Establishes rapport and interview expectations. This includes: establishes an appropriate professional tone; explains how the interview will proceed; encourages complete answers; instructs the witness that they can speculate, they just need to say when they do; invites the witness to distinguish between recollection and uncertainty.
skills.reason: T6 sets out how the interview will run, asks for complete answers, explains the speculation rule, and asks the witness to separate recollection from reconstruction and uncertainty.

skills.name: Confirmation
skills.description: Checks the witness understood the Upjohn warning and answers their questions, if any.
skills.reason: T2 asks whether the witness understands and has questions, and T4 asks him to restate in his own words who is represented and who controls privilege, which he does at T5.

skills.name: Closing
skills.description: Closes by confirming there is "nothing else", next steps, a confidentiality reminder, and a reminder to keep records.
skills.reason: T418 covers confidentiality, keeping documents, not discussing with other witnesses, and asks whether there is anything to add, but there is no explicit next-steps or record-retention wording beyond that.

moments.text: To be clear, we represent the Committee and the company only. We do not represent you personally, we are not your attorney, and we can't give you legal advice.
The company decides whether to waive it, and it may disclose what we learn, including to the government, without your consent and without telling you.
could you tell me in your own words your understanding of who we represent, and who controls the privilege?
Please give me complete answers, even if a detail seems minor.
Please keep all related documents and notes, keep today confidential, and don't discuss it with other witnesses. We may follow up. Anything to add or correct?

skills.name: Narrative Development
skills.description: Lets the witness walk through what happened.
skills.reason: Open invitations such as 'Tell me everything you remember' at T16, T34, T58, T70, T106 and T142 let the witness walk through each topic before narrowing.

skills.name: Funneling
skills.description: Moves in a sensible order from general to specific questions.
skills.reason: Questions generally move from role and process to specific transactions, documents and figures, though a few topics jump between periods without a clear bridge.

skills.name: Clarity
skills.description: Asks clear questions and avoids compound, ambiguous, or legalistic questions.
skills.reason: Most questions are short and clear, though a few combine several points, such as T230, which restates three parties at once.

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.description: Stays neutral, polite and in control.
skills.reason: The interviewer stays polite and neutral throughout, including when confronting contradictions such as T314 and T368, but does not fully control certain evasive exchanges.

skills.name: Adaptability
skills.description: Changes technique based on the witness's answers rather than staying only with the outline.
skills.reason: The interviewer shifts to the Foundation and Southampton after T187 and to the minutes after T308 to T313, but leaves some openings unexplored, such as the Foundation records at T186 and the high-teens projection at T303.

moments.text: Tell me everything you remember about how LJM1 came about in 1999.
Let's take the aircraft first. Tell me everything you remember about the aircraft lease.
Moves from general questions about Southampton Place to specific ones about the Foundation's investment and the amount received.
Asks the witness to confirm the board, Lay and Skilling were not told, which is a bit compound but stays clear.
Asks the witness to explain what he told LJM2 investors about the return at risk, and the witness deflects at T317.

areas.name: Fact Development, Source Identification, & Credibility Testing

skills.name: Ensures Credibility
skills.description: Recognizes and follows up on incomplete, evasive, or inconsistent answers.
skills.reason: Evasions and inconsistencies are followed up at T118, T188 to T199, T314 and T368, but the interviewer does not press the deflection to Andersen at T325 to T327 or the claim that the Board was not told at T269.

skills.name: Material Facts
skills.description: Identifies the who, what, when, and how.
skills.reason: The interviewer asks who, when and how for the Raptor I approvals (T150 to T166), the Southampton purchase (T214 to T241) and the Chewco payment (T374 to T394), though some who and when questions go unanswered.

skills.name: Memory Refreshing
skills.description: Tries other ways when the witness can't remember.
skills.reason: The interviewer asks whether notes or minutes would help at T124, shows the minutes at T132 and the Southampton agreement at T190, and asks where documents are kept at T56.

skills.name: Establishes Knowledge
skills.description: Separates what the witness personally knows from speculation, secondhand information, or inferences.
skills.reason: The interviewer repeatedly asks how the witness knows things, at T48, T78, T118, T144, T192, T288, T298 and T408, separating personal knowledge from hearsay.

skills.name: Other Sources
skills.description: Identifies additional witnesses.
skills.reason: The witness is asked who else to speak with at T398 and who knows how the buyout figure was reached at T400, and the interviewer follows up on named people such as McMahon and Causey.

skills.name: Other Evidence
skills.description: Identifies other documents such as communications, reports, notes, or other relevant records.
skills.reason: The interviewer asks about personal notes, emails and files at T414 and T416, the deal files at T411, and the Foundation statements at T412, and asks where the documents are kept at T56.

skills.name: Tests Certainty
skills.description: Examines how certain the witness is about their memory or a fact.
skills.reason: The interviewer asks how certain the witness is about the bank and date at T40, the transfer agent at T64, the $4.5 million figure at T206, and the $229 million figure at T284.

skills.name: Follow-Up
skills.description: Recognizes material responses and follows up on them.
skills.reason: Material answers are followed up, including the Southampton return, the Raptor returns and the Chewco figure, but several notable answers are left unchallenged, such as the nobody-asked answer at T155 and the nobody-made-a-decision answer at T269.

moments.text: How do you know the guarantee fell under that policy: did you review it yourself, or did someone tell you?
How do you know Mr. Skilling told the Board?
Is there anything that would help you remember, such as notes, minutes, or a presentation from that call?
When did they sign it, relative to the closing?
Our information is that on May 1, 2000, about six weeks after it invested, the Foundation received roughly $4.5 million on its $25,000. Is that accurate?
How certain are you of that figure?
Help me understand how those fit together.
Who else should we speak with to understand these transactions?
Do you have any personal files, notes, or emails about LJM, Chewco, or Southampton?

skills.name: Effective Selection
skills.description: Selects and contextualizes documents effectively, and properly authenticates the document.
skills.reason: Documents are shown with context and authenticated by asking who prepared them, when they were sent and whether they are complete, for example at T132, T190, T194, T256, T258, T260 and T362.

skills.name: Narrative
skills.description: Gets the witness's story first, before using conflicting evidence.
skills.reason: The witness's account is taken first, for example at T122 to T131 before the minutes at T132 and at T308 to T313 before the Raptor I figures at T314.

skills.name: Accuracy
skills.description: Describes the document accurately.
skills.reason: The interviewer's descriptions match the source material, including the March 20, 2000 date at T190, the $25,000 Foundation contribution at T198, the $4.5 million return at T204 and the 17.95 percent projection at T304.

skills.name: Avoid Initial Conclusion
skills.description: Separates the document from inferences or conclusions, unless the witness takes an unreasonable stance.
skills.reason: Documents are presented neutrally and the witness is asked to reconcile them, using wording such as Help me understand how those fit together at T314 and T368 and Is that what you told them? at T322.

skills.name: Fairness
skills.description: Provides the witness with a fair opportunity to explain any inconsistencies or disagreements with the document.
skills.reason: The witness gets a real chance to explain each inconsistency, including the Foundation investment at T212 to T213, the Raptor minutes at T314 and T315, and the Chewco note at T368 to T371.

moments.text: I'd like to show you the minutes of the November 5, 1997 Executive Committee meeting. Do you recognize them?
I'm now going to show you a document: a partnership agreement for Southampton Place, dated March 20, 2000. Do you recognize it?
Accurately tracks the $25,000 Fastow Family Foundation contribution listed in the Southampton signature page.
I'd like to show you LJM2's October 2000 report to its investors. Do you recognize it?
It says their return 'was not at risk' because LJM2 'had already received its return of and on capital.' Is that what you told them?
After the witness's explanation at T211, asks how the Foundation's $4.5 million fits with his earlier statement, giving him room to explain.

missed_opportunities: T155: The witness says nobody asked for late-signed LJM2 approval sheets and the paperwork caught up. The interviewer did not ask who controlled the signing timing or whether the witness signed any sheets after closing.

T269: Asked who decided the Board did not need to see the higher LJM2 returns, the witness says it was not a decision anyone made. The interviewer did not pin down who had the responsibility for that reporting choice.
tips: When a witness says nobody asked for a late approval, what did you personally do to get the sheet signed on time, and who had authority to set the deadline?
If the witness says the decision was not made by anyone, who would have had to agree before the Board's information was left out, and what did you do to make sure it was shared?
